subject: Re: NomadTech — economics alignment and rollout offer
messages:
From: Olivia Reed <olivia.reed@nomadtech.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Tillotson <sam.tillotson@nomadtech.com>, procurement@nomadtech.com
Date: 2027-08-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Vendor economics question: Redwood vs our incumbent

Hi Soojin —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement team asked me to get a clearer line-of-sight on the economics if we were to move inference off our current vendor. Two quick asks: 1) a head-to-head cost comparison for our observed workload (attached is a single-week sample), and 2) an outline of packaging options (prepay vs consumption) and any short-term credits you’d offer for a pilot and migration work.

We’re particularly sensitive to: token unit economics at 10k requests/day, KV-cache behaviour (we see a lot of repetition across sessions), and egress/snapshot costs during onboarding. If you can sketch an option that keeps our blended unit cost within 10% of our current spend during the first 90 days, procurement will surface to legal.

Appreciate a short proposal and a sample term sheet we can review with finance.

Best,
Olivia
Director, Platform Engineering
NomadTech

Attachment: nomadtech_usage_profile_20270805.csv (sample usage export, 7 days)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Reed <olivia.reed@nomadtech.com>
Cc: Sam Tillotson <sam.tillotson@nomadtech.com>, procurement@nomadtech.com
Date: 2027-08-05T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor economics question: Redwood vs our incumbent

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the data — landed and very helpful. Quick note before I put a short proposal together: can you confirm whether the sample includes your weekend burst and whether session affinity is sticky (per-user KV cache) or more ephemeral? That changes the projected cache hit-rate materially.

What I’ll send by EOD:
- A 90-day blended cost model (consumption and small prepay scenarios)
- Two packaging options: 1) 12-week pilot with implementation credit + consumption pricing; 2) 12-month committed band with ramped discount and a migration credit.
- An itemized list of expected onboarding egress and snapshot steps and estimated one-time fees.

If procurement has a target headroom number (e.g., maximum allowed uplift vs incumbent), tell me and I’ll bake it into the model.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_runtime_delta.xlsx (light runtime delta model for quick checks)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-05T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: NomadTech — economics alignment and rollout offer

Jordan / Marissa —

Forwarding Olivia’s note and the usage sample. Key asks: keep blended unit cost within +10% during first 90 days, and propose packaging/credits for pilot + migration. Quick thoughts below and a proposed counter we can send:

Context / risk profile:
- Heavy session repetition -> likely high KV-cache hit-rate if we align model variant/sequence length.
- Sensitive to short-term uplift during onboarding (they’ll have snapshot transfers).

Proposed public-facing counter (lean):
1) Pilot package (12 weeks):
   - $25k implementation credit (applied as invoice credit across first 60 days)
   - Consumption pricing at $0.0009 per inference-unit for pilot volume (equivalent to their 10k/day baseline)
   - One-time egress allowance of 2 TB during onboarding (billed at $0.00 up to allowance)
2) Committed package (12 months):
   - 15% discount on list per-token for a 12-month committed band based on their baseline, with a Q2 ramp (first 30 days at +5% uplift to keep margins)
   - $50k migration credit applied over first two invoices if they sign within 30 days

Operational considerations for us:
- Need product to confirm whether the egress allowance requires a special billing flag.
- Legal to sign standard SOW + short-side data processing addendum.

Marissa — can you sanity-check the margin math and propose an alternate discount if we want to protect mid-term unit economics? Jordan — if we want to sweeten the pilot without increasing long-term exposure I can pull back $10k from the migration credit and add a 30-day free trial of our advanced KV cache layer (no charge).

I’ll draft the external-facing PDF once we align.

—Soju

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Reed <olivia.reed@nomadtech.com>
Cc: Sam Tillotson <sam.tillotson@nomadtech.com>, procurement@nomadtech.com
Date: 2027-08-05T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: NomadTech — Redwood counterproposal and next steps

Hi Olivia / Sam —

Appreciate the sample data — attached is a concise counterproposal and a short-term rollout option that is designed to keep your blended cost within the +10% window during the first 90 days while preserving predictable unit economics thereafter. High-level summary: 

Headline offer
- 12-week Pilot: $25k implementation credit + consumption pricing at $0.0009 per inference-unit for pilot volume (pilot estimate based on your sample: ~10k requests/day)
- Onboarding: 2 TB egress allowance at no charge during initial snapshot transfer and first-week syncs
- Committed option: 12-month agreement with a 15% list discount and a $50k migration credit if signed within 30 days

Other notes
- We’ll enable KV-cache tuning and provide a free 30-day trial of the advanced caching layer to reduce per-token counts during the pilot window.
- If procurement needs a stricter short-term cap, we can convert part of the migration credit into a time-limited per-token rebate applied to pilot months 1–2.

Next steps
1) If this structure looks reasonable, let us know the procurement contact and we’ll share a short term sheet and embedded DocuSign for signatures.
2) We’ll run a short-run exact-cost model for your week-of-sample and attach the line-by-line run rates.

Attached: redwood_counter_20270805.pdf (summary term sheet), redwood_runtime_delta.xlsx (detailed delta model)

Would love to schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk procurement through the mechanics — feel free to propose a time.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0193
